newsitem.title: FINLAND: RESEARCH ALERT - FIM RATES STARCKJOHANN "OVERWEIGHT".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - FIM RATES STARCKJOHANN "OVERWEIGHT".

text.p: Finnish hardware and car retailer Starckjohann Oy was rated as "overweight" at brokerage FIM Securities.
Starckjohann's share at 8.20 markka level was seen appreciating 38 percent in the next 12 months, FIM said.
"Starckjohann's prospects have improved together with the pick-up in construction, increasing metal prices and growing demand on the domestic markets, " FIM said.
FIM said it sees Starckjohann's earnings this year clearly improving on 1996 and expects earnings to rise further in 1998.
FIM forecast in a research report dated January 28 Starckjohann's 1997 profit after financial items at 120 million markka versus expected 75 million in 1996.
EPS was seen at 0.89 markka in 1997 against forecast 0.55 markka in 1996.
FIM said that Starckjohann could end its debt restructuring program in the near-term and start paying dividend.
Starckjohann was forced to enter a debt restructuring program in 1993, but the program does not substantially boost the company's earnings anymore, it said.
In addition, the company is not not allowed to pay dividend while under debt restructuring program.
The faith of banking group Merita's large holding in Starckjohann was seen as a risk.
"Rapid growth in the supply side can have a negative effect on market stability," FIM said.
Merita held 55.2 percent of Starckjohann at end 1996.
